rule.description: One policy — the baseline environment every sandbox-executed process observes — is fragmented across dedicated per-file fragment-owner functions, and each consumer hand-merges whichever fragments apply. The baseline is judged fragmented when fragment owners live in three or more distinct files of the orchestrator crate.

checks.description: Detect dedicated functions that privately assemble a share of the sandbox execution-environment baseline from their own literals and hand it to callers as a pair collection (or write it into the live process environment).
checks.detected_relation: fragment owner function -> environment name/value pairs assembling one piece of the shared baseline
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Each owner is where one conceptual setting of a single policy lives; with one policy decided in five different files, any revision of the baseline requires finding and editing each owner.

matches.evidence: Associated function on the wire request type returning CARGO_TERM_COLOR=never and LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 from its own literals (owner span reported at src/message.rs:149).
Free function in the resource-limits module returning a map holding CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 and CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true (owner span reported at src/coordinator/limits.rs:20).
Free function next to the request lowerings returning a map that conditionally holds RUST_BACKTRACE=1 (owner span reported at src/coordinator.rs:2408).
Free function in the process-spawning module returning a vector holding PLAYGROUND_SANDBOX=1 and TZ=UTC (owner span reported at src/worker.rs:411).
Binary-startup function that writes TZ (defaulting to UTC) and PLAYGROUND_WORKER=1 into the live process environment before the worker listens (owner span reported at src/bin/worker.rs:10).

checks.description: Detect functions that call any fragment owner, i.e. places that must know which fragments exist and which subset applies to what they run.
checks.detected_relation: consumer function -> fragment owner function it merges into the command environment
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Every consumer is a site that must be revisited, in step with the owners and with each other, whenever the baseline or the composition of a request's environment changes; the coordination cost of the dispersed policy lives here.

matches.evidence: Run-request lowering merges the run-detail, fairness, and rendering fragments in order (consumer span reported at src/coordinator.rs:483).
Compile-request lowering merges the run-detail, fairness, and rendering fragments in order (consumer span reported at src/coordinator.rs:592).
Format-request lowering merges only the rendering fragment into a fresh map (consumer span reported at src/coordinator.rs:692).
Clippy-request lowering merges only the rendering fragment into a fresh map (consumer span reported at src/coordinator.rs:740).
Miri-request lowering keeps its own miri variables and merges the rendering fragment on top (consumer span reported at src/coordinator.rs:789).
Macro-expansion lowering merges only the rendering fragment into a fresh map (consumer span reported at src/coordinator.rs:858).
The process-spawning loop floors every started process with the sandbox fragment via entry().or_insert so coordinator-sent keys still win (consumer span reported at src/worker.rs:581).
The binary entrypoint seeds the worker's inherited environment by calling the startup fragment before listening (consumer span reported at src/bin/worker.rs:17).

excluded.why: Tool-specific request data, not baseline policy; its enclosing function's declared return type is the request type, so it is neither an owner under the rule nor silently credited.

excluded.what: The SpliceEnvironment glue trait and its two impls
excluded.why: Pure merge plumbing with no baseline settings of its own; it is reachable through the consumer matches and disappears with the topology, not an independent location of the smell.
They carry name/value pairs over the wire but decide none of them; only the rendering_contract accessor attached to one message type is baseline policy.
